questions.q: Why do institutions exist, according to Pinker?
a: To help flawed people stay objective and live in peace
To reward the most intelligent members of society
To replace personal morality with strict laws
To protect the interests of the wealthy
questions.why: Lesson 1 says institutions exist because humans are not naturally objective or considerate.

questions.q: Why does the summary say we behave morally?
a: Because it is rational and serves our well-being
Because we are naturally selfless from birth
Because institutions force us to comply
Because guilt is stronger than reason
questions.why: Lesson 2 argues morality is the rational choice for social animals who benefit from society.

questions.q: What makes self-constraint a rational strategy?
a: Avoiding temptation works better than trusting willpower
It proves to others that you are disciplined
It removes the need for any planning
It increases your tolerance for bad habits
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the safest way to resist a treat is not to put yourself near it.

questions.q: Which example does the summary give of useful ignorance?
a: Choosing not to learn whether you will develop an illness
Ignoring a doctor's advice about treatment
Refusing to read the news every morning
Skipping all annual lab tests for prevention
questions.why: Lesson 3 discusses weighing whether knowing your genetic risk would only make life harder.

questions.q: What does the summary say sets humans apart from other species?
a: The ability to reason and overcome obstacles
The instinct to protect their young
The capacity to feel fear and pain
The need to live in social groups
questions.why: The overview says rationality, or using reason to change circumstances, separates us from animals.
